candidate.blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Health Promotion and Maintenance, printed p.9 / PDF p.13
candidate.educational_objective: Teach the key home-safety facts about radon and the need for testing.

options.A: Radon is an invisible, odorless radioactive gas and home testing is the only way to know whether levels are elevated.
options.B: Radon can be reliably detected by smell.
options.C: Radon is not associated with lung cancer.
options.D: Radon testing is unnecessary outside a few rare locations because elevated levels have not been found nationwide.

candidate.rationale: EPA describes radon as a naturally occurring radioactive gas that cannot be seen or smelled. Radon is the second leading cause of lung cancer in the United States, and testing is the only way to determine whether a home has elevated radon levels.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Radon cannot be detected by human senses; home testing is necessary to identify elevated levels and reduce lung-cancer risk.
candidate.source_document_title: Radon in Homes, Schools and Buildings
candidate.source_locator: Radiation Facts / What You Can Do—radon invisible and odorless; second leading cause of lung cancer; test to determine level
